thread:
Maria: Quick heads-up — after the runtime deploy (yesterday evening) I'm seeing odd batch shapes for the short-seq traffic. Metrics look like more small batches and higher tail latency.
Kevin: Can you drop the snapshot? :eyes:
Maria: pasted below from the dashboard (5m window):
```
batch_utilization: 0.58
avg_tokens_per_batch: 47
median_queue_depth: 3
kv_hitrate: 0.61
tokens_per_sec: 12.4k
95latency_ms: 210
99latency_ms: 470
small_batch_rate(<32 tokens): 42%
```
Maria: Note that before deploy avg_tokens_per_batch was ~86 and kv_hitrate ~0.74. KV miss rate jumped ~30%.
Ali: Hmm — did the queue policy change the token budget cap or fill timeout? I remember we tightened token_budget_threshold from 0.9 -> 0.75 in the rollout.
Sasha: Yup, that commit (deploy-2026-09-12) lowered target token utilization to reduce worst-case GPU memory spikes. Might be starving batch formation for short requests.
Kevin: If token budget lowered, we probably shifted to earlier flushes which produce smaller batches and erode KV cache reuse. Fewer multi-request sequences hit the same cache.
Maria: I ran a microprofile against the runtime on a worker with the new config — attaching snippet:
```
PROFILE: continuous-batcher:trace_id=0x7a
- enqueue_delay_p50: 4.2ms
- fill_time_p50: 18.6ms
- flush_by_token_budget: 38%
- flush_by_timeout: 62%
- avg_batch_size: 3.1 requests
- avg_tokens_per_batch: 45
- kvcache_local_hits: 121k
- kvcache_local_misses: 78k
```
Maria: Compared to baseline, kvcache_local_hits dropped ~35k in same window.
Sasha: That matches the dashboard. Also saw a small kernel fallback for fused-attn on a subset of sequences around 512 tokens — could be affecting throughput per-token.
Ali: Two moving parts then: queue token budget causing smaller batches, and kernel selection fallback slightly slowing hot paths. Both reduce tokens/sec and hurt tail latency.
Kevin: Proposal: revert token_budget_threshold to 0.9 for the short-seq priority queue and add a soft cap by wall-clock fill_time_ms (e.g., 40ms) to avoid long stalls. Also enable the new fused-attn-v2 for seq>256 only after we validate coverage.
Maria: I like that. We should also add telemetry counters for "flush_reason" (token_budget | timeout | capacity) per-queue and expose per-kernel latency histograms so we can detect those fallbacks in dashboards.
Sasha: I'll add a small probe to the runtime to emit kernel_choice and kvcache_hop (local|remote|miss) tags on the batching spans. Minimal perf impact.
Ali: For dashboards: add a stacked bar for flush_reason over time, and a scatter of avg_tokens_per_batch vs tokens/sec. Also surface kvcache_hitrate per-model and per-route — the regressions appear route-specific (chat-short vs summarization).
Kevin: Can someone run an A/B with the reverted token_budget_threshold on one dedicated pool? We should measure dp95/dp99 and tokens/sec before we change prod-wide. Ops-bot: create canary pool job? @ops-bot
ops-bot: created canary pool "batchshape-canary-01" with token_budget_threshold=0.9 and fill_time_ms_softcap=40. Job id: canary-2026-09-13-77
Maria: Running synthetic replay against canary now (~30k reqs). Initial numbers after 10m:
```
canary batch_utilization: 0.74
canary avg_tokens_per_batch: 81
canary kv_hitrate: 0.72
canary tokens_per_sec: 18.5k
canary 95latency_ms: 180
```
Maria: Looks promising. Tail still needs checking.
Kevin: Great. After 1h canary, run a perf profile to confirm no kernel regressions. Sasha, tag the telemetry for kernel_choice during the canary.
Sasha: Will do. Also adding an alert rule: if kv_hitrate drops >10% vs baseline for a route, page SRE and flag the rollout.
Ali: Next steps: 1) keep canary running 2) collect 1h of traces including kernel_choice and flush_reason 3) evaluate dp95/dp99 + tokens/sec + cost delta 4) if positive, rollout to small % of traffic then ramp.
Maria: Agreed. I'll post updates here with the 1h dashboard and the profiling flamegraphs. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
